nodes.label: Behavior-First Fingerprinting
nodes.rationale: Names, ordering in UI, and cosmetic properties change frequently and are not reliable signals of functional intent. Behavioral properties are the only stable basis for standards governance and drift detection.

nodes.label: Deterministic, Auditable Hashes
nodes.rationale: Hashes without explainability cannot be trusted or debugged. Auditability is mandatory for governance and standards enforcement.

nodes.label: record_rows as Canonical Explainability
nodes.rationale: Lists of names or counts are insufficient for traceability. A stable (record_key → sig_hash) mapping enables diffs, audits, and downstream tooling.

nodes.label: UniqueId Usage Is Restricted
nodes.rationale: Blind use of UniqueId causes unnecessary churn and false drift. Some domains are definition-based, not identity-based.

nodes.label: Fail-Soft Is Mandatory
nodes.rationale: Silence hides risk. Explicit failure markers preserve state distinctions and auditability.

nodes.label: Ordering Rules Are Explicit Per Domain
nodes.rationale: Some structures (e.g. view filter stacks) are order-dependent; others are not. Implicit ordering leads to accidental semantic changes.

nodes.label: Global vs Contextual Domain Split
nodes.rationale: Duplication of global definitions inside views/templates causes inconsistency and waste.

nodes.label: View Templates Are Behavioral, Not Nominal
nodes.rationale: Two templates with the same name can behave differently. Name-only fingerprints are misleading and unsafe.

nodes.label: Views Compose Templates + Deltas
nodes.rationale: This mirrors actual Revit behavior and avoids double-counting settings.

nodes.label: Phase Names in Behavioral Hashes
nodes.rationale: UniqueIds are document-specific and cannot be compared across projects. Phase names provide the semantic link needed for cross-project drift detection.

nodes.label: Domain-Driven Architecture
nodes.rationale: This enables refactoring, selective execution, and future portability.

nodes.label: Markdown Portability Rule
nodes.rationale: GitHub Mobile, Obsidian, and chat renderers handle nested fences inconsistently.

nodes.label: Phase Graphics Domain Disabled (API Limitation)
nodes.rationale: Avoids misleading fingerprints and false confidence.

nodes.label: Hash Mode Migration Timeline
nodes.rationale: Setting explicit criteria prevents indefinite deferral while protecting against premature switching.

nodes.label: Domain Family Split Architecture
nodes.rationale: Monolithic extractors mixed heterogeneous record structures, making per-class policy governance impractical.

nodes.label: View Category Overrides Scope and Category Classification
nodes.rationale: This mirrors actual Revit behavior and avoids double-counting settings.

nodes.label: line_patterns Join Key Upgraded to Scale-Invariant Normalized Segments
nodes.rationale: Governance identity for line patterns is structural type, not absolute scale.

nodes.label: loaded_family_types scope: loaded families only; system families deferred
nodes.rationale: This creates real tension with this project's own non-negotiable rule.
